metadata.title: Email Threat Protection
metadata.description: Defines trust properties required to detect, block, and respond to malicious or deceptive email content. This pattern addresses phishing, malware, weaponized links, and social engineering delivered via email, and does not address identity governance, data classification, or records retention.

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for detecting, blocking, and responding to malicious or deceptive email content targeting users and systems.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Email security gateways, content inspection, attachment analysis, link analysis, and incident response workflows.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for preventing, detecting, and responding to email-based threats such as phishing, malware, and business email compromise.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: Email threat protection assumes baseline delivery assurance, identity binding, and authenticated transport are already enforced.

props.name: data-object
props.remarks: Email messages and attachments as security-relevant information objects requiring inspection and response.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for trustworthy email guidance related to monitoring, detection, and response to malicious or deceptive email activity.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced for guidance on identifying and mitigating phishing, malicious attachments, and weaponized links in email systems.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Referenced to emphasize threat detection, response, and adaptation as core cyber resiliency functions for institutional email.

metadata.remarks: Email Threat Protection reduces institutional risk from phishing, malware, and social engineering delivered through email by enforcing detection, analysis, and response without altering sender identity governance or data classification.

components.title: Phishing and Social Engineering Detection
components.description: Detects deceptive email messages intended to manipulate recipients into unsafe actions.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Phishing via email messages, links, or attachments.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: User execution triggered by deceptive email content.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Inspection and analysis of email content to identify deceptive or malicious elements.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Email content is examined to detect and block malicious or deceptive messages.
Email activity is monitored to identify indicators of phishing and social engineering.

components.title: Malicious Attachment and Link Protection
components.description: Identifies and mitigates malware and exploit delivery through email attachments and embedded links.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Malicious file execution initiated via email attachments.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Ingress tool transfer via embedded links or payloads in email.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Pre-delivery detonation and analysis of email attachments and linked content.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Email attachments and links are assessed for malicious code prior to user access.
External threat intelligence informs identification of malicious email artifacts.

components.title: Email Incident Detection and Response
components.description: Supports rapid identification, containment, and remediation of email-based security incidents.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Compromise and abuse of valid email accounts.

props.name: defensive-technique
props.remarks: Detection, alerting, and coordinated response to email-based threats.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Email-related incidents are analyzed, contained, and eradicated.
Automated response mechanisms may be used to contain malicious email activity.
